# Branch names a workflow is allowed to reference BEFORE the branch exists.
#
# A `branches:` filter is a union: naming several branches adds matches, it never
# removes them. So naming a branch that does not exist yet is harmless *provided
# the default branch is also named* -- the default branch is what gates CI, and
# it is the one omission that makes a workflow unfireable.
#
# That is the whole reason this file exists. Without it, a workflow naming only
# a nonexistent branch is a green badge over zero jobs, and that is how
# quilt-jetson's CI spent its entire history: `branches: [main]` in a repository
# whose default branch is `master`.
#
# scripts/ci_trigger_guard.py fails on any phantom branch that is not declared
# here. Keep this list short, and justify each entry.
#
# 38% of this account's repositories default to `main` and the rest to `master`,
# so a workflow that names only one of them is dead in a third of the fleet.
main
